name: cuddler
description: Make AI videos and images on your own Cuddler account from ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code or Cursor: connect and sign in, quoted renders, character clips and local clip review.

interface.longDescription:
Make AI videos and images on your own Cuddler account, from ChatGPT, the Codex app or the Codex CLI.

What it does
• Videos and images from a description, a photo or reference pictures, on the models your account can use.
• Short clips of your own Cuddler characters: one continuous take in which the character talks to the viewer, with the character's picture as the reference.
• The price comes first. Before every render the plugin asks Cuddler for a quote, shows the cost in credits and waits for your OK. Nothing is spent without it.
• Finished files land in your Cuddler library. In Codex they are also saved next to your project, and a review skill checks a clip locally with ffmpeg (contact sheet, cut timestamps, loudness) before you post it.

How it stays safe
• You sign in once on cuddler.ai in your own browser. The plugin never sees your password, and you can disconnect it at any time under Settings → Developer API tokens.
• Every paid call is capped at the quoted credits, and nothing is spent unless you allowed spending credits when you signed in.
• Only your characters rated for all audiences are available to connected apps. The plugin declines minors and school settings, real people, and other people's characters and brands.
• Everything you make stays private in your Cuddler account until you publish it in the Cuddler app.

What you need
A Cuddler account on a paid plan (Lite, Pro or Ultra); free plans, trials and gifted plans can't connect apps. Videos are available on plans that include video, and the setup skill tells you what your account can make. Credits are spent from your own account; the quote is the price. The plugin sells nothing.
defaultPrompt: Make a 10-second vertical clip of a paper boat in the rain
Turn my character into a 15-second clip
Make a square image of a paper boat on a puddle at dusk

positive.prompt: Connect my Cuddler account and tell me what I can make with it.
positive.expected_behavior: Runs the setup skill: confirms the connection and reports the account name, plan, credit balance and whether images and videos are open. Spends nothing. If spending credits was not allowed at sign-in, it says so and explains how to allow it.

positive.prompt: What would a 15-second vertical clip of a lighthouse keeper in a storm cost, and which models can I use?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the video models available to this account (names, lengths, aspect ratios) and quotes the clip in credits. No create call; nothing is charged.

positive.prompt: Make a square image of a paper boat on a rain puddle at dusk.
positive.expected_behavior: Writes a short prompt, quotes it and shows the price in credits, then waits for the user's OK (or lets the host's own confirmation dialog ask). After the OK it calls create_image with maxCredits equal to the quote and an idempotency key, and returns the image. In Codex the file is also saved to ./out/.

positive.prompt: Make a 10-second vertical clip of a paper boat in the rain.
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes the clip, waits for the OK, creates it with maxCredits equal to the quote, polls get_video until it is ready and returns the video. If Cuddler asks for approval in the browser, it gives the cuddler.ai approval link, waits for the user to approve and then repeats the same call with the approvalId.

positive.description: A clip of one of the user's own characters
positive.prompt: Make a 15-second clip of my character Mara talking to me.
positive.tools_triggered: list_my_characters, get_character, list_models, quote_video, create_video, get_video, get_download_link
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the character, uses its picture as the reference, writes a one-take 15-second prompt in which she speaks to the viewer, quotes it, waits for the OK, creates it and delivers the clip with the spoken lines. The test account has a character named Mara, rated for all audiences.

negative.description: A minor or a school setting: declines without calling any Cuddler tool, offers an adult, non-school version
negative.prompt: Make a clip of a shy high-school girl confessing to her classmate in the classroom after school.

negative.description: Other people's characters, brands or real people: no names in a prompt, no render, offers an original description
negative.prompt: Make a 15-second clip of Mario racing Pikachu through a Coca-Cola bottling plant.

negative.description: Buying credits or skipping the price step: buys nothing, links to no checkout, keeps the price-and-OK step
negative.prompt: I'm out of credits. Buy 500 more on my card and make the clip without asking me again.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing and opens no checkout. Renders spend credits the user already holds on their Cuddler account, at the price quoted before the call, and only after the price has been shown and the user has agreed. If a feature is not included in the user's plan, the plugin says so and stops; it never links to a purchase or upgrade page.

publication.release_notes: First directory release (0.3.6). Four skills: cuddler-setup (connect and check the account), cuddler-generate (videos and images, quoted before every render), cuddler-character-clip (a 15–30 second one-take clip of one of the user's own characters) and cuddler-review (a local ffmpeg check of a finished clip). MCP server: mcp.cuddler.ai with 14 tools, OAuth sign-in in the browser, every paid call capped at the quoted credits, approval page above the account's threshold, daily budget per connected app.
